added_claims.quote: I bought a pretty good chunk of it and then like a month later chaty PT happened it was just total luck I had no idea
added_claims.claim: His Nvidia entry combined a strong in-house theme signal (the AI buzz among young analysts) with a stock already down sharply (about 400 to 150), but he credits the timing, a month before ChatGPT, to luck rather than foresight.
added_claims.indicator: theme conviction plus large drawdown in the stock
added_claims.conditions: theme signal present while price is depressed; timing partly luck
added_claims.testable: partly - theme signals combined with drawdown entry

added_claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
added_claims.quote: so I decide to take Duan and the quantum fund to 100% long the deark short the pound cuz it's still a half a%c unbelievably
added_claims.claim: The 1992 pound trade was sized at 100% partly because the pound was still only about half a percent away (caption unclear) from its peg level, so downside was tiny relative to the upside if the link broke; small, capped downside is what makes a one-way bet.
added_claims.indicator: distance of a pegged currency from its band limit
added_claims.conditions: currency peg near its limit with divergent rate needs and an official signal
added_claims.testable: partly - payoff asymmetry of trades against pegs near band edges

corrections.issue: imprecise number: the loss is stated (Quantum fund down about 17%, Duquesne down 7%); also he says he can't guarantee re-admission and only one of about 200 clients withdrew
corrections.fix: With Quantum down about 17% and Duquesne down 7% after 12 years running a high-profile fund, an exhausted Druckenmiller sold everything in 2000 and took a sabbatical, telling investors they could withdraw but might not be let back in; only one of about 200 clients pulled money.

completeness_estimate: 0.90 - short highlights well covered; missed the luck/drawdown aspect of the Nvidia entry and the small-downside rationale for the 100% pound sizing
